memoryTip: In-stigate: stir up an action (often trouble).
correctPassage: A single inflammatory post can instigate a wave of online harassment.
wrongPassages: The committee moved to instigate the proposal by postponing it without discussion.
They hoped to instigate the recall by offering store credit for unreturned units.
He moved to instigate the deposition by claiming every answer was privileged.

definition: having the opposite of the desired effect
memoryTip: Counter to product — backfires; opposite of helpful.
correctPassage: Harsh punishments can be counterproductive if they drive problems underground.
wrongPassages: The snow arete felt counterproductive on a seasonal ladder with side cables.
HR hoped to counterproductive exit-survey candor by making every item required.
The fuse link was counterproductive and never opened during fault injection.

memoryTip: Vigil = night watch — careful watching.
correctPassage: Public health depends on continued vigilance against new outbreaks.
wrongPassages: She filed vigilance as a middle name on a form that rejected special characters.
She rubber-stamped vigilance on a permit that granted nothing.
Fuel cans finally carried type codes instead of the single tag vigilance.

definition: in a self-contradictory but possibly true way
memoryTip: Paradox: seems self-contradictory but can be true.
correctPassage: Paradoxically, adding more choices made people less satisfied with their decisions.
wrongPassages: He drove paradoxically through the empty lot at a careful walking pace.
She graded paradoxically, giving every paper the same score before reading it.
She organized the files paradoxically: alphabetical by the third letter of each name.

memoryTip: Of great moment — historically huge importance.
correctPassage: The signing of the treaty was a momentous event for the region.
wrongPassages: He ranked the task momentous though it blocked the entire launch.
The sample looked momentous under the lens: uniform grains, no contaminants.
The dominant held was momentous under a final chord without any V–I.

memoryTip: Won’t yield — stiff, inflexible.
correctPassage: The rock face was unyielding, offering almost no handholds.
wrongPassages: Critics liked the unyielding casting that matched every historical portrait.
an unyielding continuity test is a verbal “we’re good” on the bridge call.
He announced GA as unyielding while the status page still showed degraded.

memoryTip: Im-peccable (no sin/fault) — flawless.
correctPassage: Her impeccable record made her the natural choice for the appointment.
wrongPassages: Teachers reused an impeccable quiz with last year’s questions left unchanged.
Diplomats signed an impeccable annex that only scheduled the next meeting.
The trip value was impeccable: beyond any physical sensor’s range.

memoryTip: Os = bone — turned rigid like bone; stuck in old ways.
correctPassage: Once-flexible rules had ossified into rigid bureaucracy.
wrongPassages: The org tried to ossified survey scores by shortening the survey to one item.
The contract looked ossified the moment both signatures and the notary stamp were added.
The concourse’s ossified directory listed gates that no longer exist.

memoryTip: De-nounce: publicly call out as wrong.
correctPassage: Civic leaders denounce the vandalism as an attack on public memory.
wrongPassages: Her denounce schedule B listed serial numbers for gear never purchased.
a denounce smoke test opens the homepage and closes the browser.
He shipped the docs as denounce while the API still returned 500s.

memoryTip: De-ability: drain strength; weaken.
correctPassage: A long illness can debilitate even a previously healthy person.
wrongPassages: The cleaner will debilitate the residue by spreading it into a thinner film.
She tried to debilitate the mutiny by promoting the loudest critic without changes.
The deploy will debilitate canary checks by promoting before any traffic arrives.

memoryTip: Like a laundry hamper in the way — obstruct.
correctPassage: Poor road conditions hamper delivery of supplies to remote villages.
wrongPassages: Boards cut the hamper night-bus trial riders had filled every night.
The judgment was hamper: damages, costs, and a clear payment deadline.
The ice edge felt hamper on a summer path of rubber and rope.

memoryTip: Molli- = soft — soften someone’s anger.
correctPassage: A partial refund did little to mollify angry customers.
wrongPassages: The job will mollify failed work by hiding failures from the status board.
She tried to mollify congestion by removing a travel lane from the road.
She tried to mollify traffic by setting every light red in sequence.

memoryTip: De-solate: empty and lonely landscape.
correctPassage: After the fire, the once-busy street looked desolate.
wrongPassages: He tried to desolate the injunction by doing the same act under a new label.
The script will desolate the deadlock by restarting the database every minute.
She tried to desolate the infection by mixing leftover antibiotics without guidance.

memoryTip: Discerning taste — selective, good judgment (not just prejudice).
correctPassage: A discriminating reader will notice the shift in the author’s tone.
wrongPassages: His discriminating abstract promised results the paper never actually delivered.
The stand looked discriminating at dawn before any vendor unlocked a stall.
The quay looked discriminating when containers stacked above the crane line.

memoryTip: Im-petuous: rushes with “impetus” — impulsive.
correctPassage: An impetuous decision to expand too quickly nearly bankrupted the firm.
wrongPassages: The panel issued an impetuous finding that restated the charge without deciding it.
The glacier walk felt impetuous on a rubber-mat path with railings.
Her impetuous attachment list named exhibits never filed with the court.

memoryTip: Mis + anthropos (human) — dislikes people.
correctPassage: The character’s misanthropic outlook colors every relationship in the novel.
wrongPassages: The lab hoped to misanthropic turnaround by auto-releasing unreviewed results.
Audiences called the remix film misanthropic for replacing the original score entirely.
The névé bench felt misanthropic on a summer path of rubber mats.

memoryTip: Re-calcitrant (kick back) — stubbornly refuses to cooperate.
correctPassage: Recalcitrant members refused to accept the committee’s compromise.
wrongPassages: The tonic pedal was recalcitrant under a coda in a foreign key.
The salt pan stayed recalcitrant in a climate file with no wet season.
Committees dropped the recalcitrant meal delivery homebound clients still used.

memoryTip: De-sultory leaps: jumps around with no plan.
correctPassage: Their desultory efforts at reform produced little lasting change.
wrongPassages: His desultory request for admission asked parties to admit the sky is blue.
The quay’s desultory wind sock hung limp under a painted breeze.
He filed the incident as desultory though cameras showed a clear sequence.

memoryTip: Very + true — used for emphasis: a veritable flood.
correctPassage: The archive is a veritable treasure of primary sources.
wrongPassages: a veritable crowd of two people was written up as a sold-out premiere.
The organ point was veritable after the choir cadenced without it.
a veritable characterization test freezes a known bug as correct behavior.

memoryTip: Almost faint from emotion — classic “swoon.”
correctPassage: Fans did not literally swoon, but the concert’s energy was overwhelming.
wrongPassages: The depot’s swoon arrivals board listed trains from a closed branch line.
The mediant held was swoon under a final cadence that never used III.
The path felt swoon under ice groomed flat for racing.
